stem: Immediately before starting a blood transfusion, which patient-identification action is essential?

options.A: Use at least two person-specific identifiers and match the intended blood product to the identified patient
options.B: Use the room number as the only identifier if the patient is familiar to the nurse
options.C: Rely on the blood bank's earlier verification without identifying the patient again at the point of care
options.D: Use the blood-product unit number alone as proof of the patient's identity

rationale: The Joint Commission's current patient-identification requirement calls for reliable identification using two person-specific identifiers before care, treatment, or services and matching the intended treatment to that individual. Room number is not an acceptable identifier. Blood-product labeling and prior laboratory verification do not replace point-of-care patient identification.
educational_objective: Prevent transfusion identification errors by using two person-specific patient identifiers and matching the intended blood product to the correct patient at the point of care.
source_document_title: Two Patient Identifiers — Understanding the Requirements; National Performance Goal #1: Right Patient, Right Care
source_locator: Standards FAQ 000001463 > Intent, identifiers, temporary names; National Performance Goal #1
source_claim_supported: Use two person-specific identifiers to reliably identify the patient and match treatment/services to that patient; room number is not an acceptable identifier, and patient identifiers are used to match against blood-product labels.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
correction_summary: Removed the unsupported absolute claim that two staff members must always perform the bedside check. Reframed the item around the current, publicly verifiable patient-identification requirement that is invariant across manual and electronic verification workflows.
audit_findings: A reflects the current patient-identification standard. B uses a prohibited identifier; C omits point-of-care patient identification; D identifies the product rather than the patient. No second answer remains.
